quest.title: Those We Have Kept
quest.description: Now that she has been "born anew," what will she choose to do next...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali sure drank a lot last night, huh... Wonder if she's even awake...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Good morning.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waah! C—Columbina! You, uh, sure know how to make an entrance... What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: We just finished filming a last-minute scene, so I came up to get some fresh air.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: The others are still down below discussing what the final scene should be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, how it should end?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes. They're torn between whether the heroine should reunite with her old friend or not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... Because the whole point is that she came to her friend's homeland to search for her, right? Paimon almost forgot the plot...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes. Director Furina and Miss Chiori think a tragic ending where the two never meet would be more poignant.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: But Director Xavier thinks having the two reunite would make for a more touching and heartwarming ending.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Me? I... I'm not sure...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: On a personal level, of course I want to see her again... of course I want to experience that moment where we reunite... even if it's just for the Kameras.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: But that means... an actor would have to take her place, and that makes me feel...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't stress about that for now.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Don't look so worried! Making a film is supposed to be fun!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—Besides, it's all gonna work out! You can trust Paimon on that!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Work out... how?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, well... Y'know...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It'll all get tied up in a nice little bow. You'll see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Exactly!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hehe... Okay. I trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I'll just focus on having fun for now.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: #Well, well, look who we have here! {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Aw, the lighting specialist and clapper loader that never were...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah... We kinda went AWOL didn't we. Sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hehe, seriously, don't worry about it. Everything's going smoothly on our end, so just do what you need to do.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: You seem to be in better spirits now, Miss Columbina. I apologize if our earlier discussion put you on the spot...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: #It's okay, I'm fine now. {NICKNAME} and Paimon talked me through it.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: So, what are your thoughts on the ending then? Should we have them reunite or not?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: We should... tie everything up in bows.

choices.text: We'll definitely make it up to you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, right on time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, yeah... We weren't the ones who drank our weight in alcohol yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Heh, what? Are you suggesting granny can't handle her liquor? It takes a lot more than that to get me drunk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? 'Cause, uh, you stopped making sense after a while...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Uh... Did I? Huh, news to me. I didn't say anything... too crazy, I hope.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... You spent half an hour badmouthing Ororon, half an hour complaining about work, an hour talking about light novels... and, uh, Paimon kinda fell asleep after that.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Are they gone?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm? Oh, the crew? Yeah, we bumped into them on the deck, but they just left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait but, now that everything with your core is sorted out, what's stopping you from seeing Columbina? She misses you a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I... I just want to deal with this mess first. Besides, this is the perfect chance to make her jump for once. I have to plan it out more.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But, enough about that. Were you able to pinpoint the location of our target?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course. When Granny Itztli promises something, she delivers!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Great, let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The Morte Region... Wait, this is the Tower of Gestalt.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The place the souls were severed... Is that the source of the resentment? Or is it the Narzissenkreuz Ordo in general?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let me come with. This thing's movement isn't fixed. If it's not at this location when we get there, I can use a ritual to summon it.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You've already gone to more than enough trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I don't mind. These old bones have nothing better to do anyway. Summoning a spirit isn't going to do me in.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Besides, if I don't go, they'll just have more inside jokes I can't join in on!)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright then. I appreciate it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, there's no time to lose. Let's head out!

talks.objective: Head to the Tower of Gestalt
Check the space within the Tower of Gestalt

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh, no sign of it so far...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Should I start the summoning ritual?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Let's drain the water from this floor of the tower first. It'll make it easier to move around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, we can do that?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Of course. Alain and Rene both saw the future that awaited Fontaine, and even shared a few methods for waterproofing buildings. The principle behind it is...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Ahem, not important. Just unlock the mechanisms in the order I tell you.

talks.objective: Empty the Tower of Gestalt of water
Wait for Citlali to start the ritual

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ready?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yeah. When this thing appears, I'll try talking to the souls inside.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But, more than likely, they've already been driven to madness. If communication fails, we'll have a battle on our hands.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, Paimon better find a hiding spot.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: If a fight does break out, I should be the one to deliver the final blow. Trust me on that.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, I need quiet.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Wandering spirits drifting along the tides, hear me now. Broken souls, silenced, torn apart, and forsaken, follow the traces of the past and return to us.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Let resentment recognize resentment. Let vile entities be drawn together, and in this place, take form once more!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (...What now? Is that it?)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Ugh... This is exactly why I deal in math not magic. How are we supposed to know what stage the spell is at? It's like there's no logic to speak of.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Mechanical science is so much easier to—)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hey, you! Or whoever's inside of you... I need you to listen to me.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm a descendant of Fontaine's "Lord-Artificer," Alain Guillotin. I can make you whole again and return you to the Ley Lines. You just need to work with me here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sandrone!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch... Looks like talking this out is off the table.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, plan B... Time to blow off some steam!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Is it over?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yep. Told you it'd be a piece of cake.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: How did you do that back there?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That creature was nothing special. Add a bunch of souls with nowhere to go, a touch of malicious energy, a few impurities, and a whole lot of resentment, and that's what you get.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: All I did was separate the original souls from the rest of the filth, allowing them to be accepted by the current rules of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The principle behind the world-formula is "divergence." Starting from a point of origin, it deconstructs and reconstructs the possibilities of the world to find certain answers.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So, it would follow that reverse-calculating the world-formula allows us to achieve convergence and restoration instead. Using the numerological array, I was able to do just that.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's similar to the concept of homological reduction in mathematics. I reduced them to the basic, fundamental essence of their being, without changing their underlying nature.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That meant... Ugh, never mind. Judging by all the blank stares, I'm guessing you don't actually care.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I think I finally understand how outlanders feel when I ramble on about Shaman stuff...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: P—Point is, it was super impressive! You really are amazing, Sandrone!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hah, you're just realizing that now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd expect nothing less from the Unraveller of All Reason...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ahem, enough about that!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: W—We should get going! I'll go reset the mechanisms inside the tower. See you back on land!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well, that's one old mess for the books. Glad to have that over and done with.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Feels nice to do a good deed every once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You helped everyone out a bunch in Nod-Krai, too! Kinda seems like you're just a good person at heart!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh, I wouldn't be so sure. I'll be heading back to the Fatui soon enough. You two are too trusting sometimes...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, at the very least, we know we can trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmph, fine. Just don't say I didn't warn you when it comes back to bite you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, where to next? Back to the ship?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Your personal business, the Narzissenkreuz thing, it's all resolved. That means you can "see the people that need seeing" now, right Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone's gonna be so happy you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh... You wouldn't catch me dead admitting to this before, but... Yeah. I really have missed everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Columbina's a special case, though! This time, I'm definitely getting her back for all her annoying antics over the years!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Um, Sandrone...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Don't ruin the moment. Or I'll start thinking about how you teleported me to a random location after I explicitly told you to stop doing that...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: U—Um...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Aaand... Scene! Bravo! Bravo! We got it! This is exactly the ending I was hoping for!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Where did you just go, Miss Columbina? You vanished, and then the next second you were back, hugging this, um... new friend here.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Th—That... was all... on... Kamera...?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Yeah. Well, the Kamera was already rolling, and it happened so fast, so... Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hold on, this must be...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yep, my best friend. The one I was looking for. I never thought I'd actually get to see her again. I'm just... so happy.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Plus, the film got a happy ending too. It's all thanks to you, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: ...Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You couldn't stop being annoying for one second!? Columbinaaaa!
